## Historical audit — S0346, chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_92056365/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | H was asked to reconstruct an indoor photograph using separate meshes and a matching camera. The inferred scene goal is a restaurant interior, based on H’s inventory, not an independent image inspection (lines 1, 3). |
| First build | H emitted multiple named assets: architecture, booths, tables, chairs, pendants and plants. Chairs have separate backs, seats and supports; pendants have cords, collars and shades. Chair rotations encode pose. Colors and geometric seams are specified, but texture and physical connections are not independently verified (lines 3–4). |
| Validation | Step 1 built and rendered successfully; its foreground table landmark projected to (0.03, 1.16), versus H’s reference estimate (0.45, 0.99). This is a point-projection discrepancy, not proof of a visible contour mismatch (lines 6–9). |
| Review and revision | H reported a cropped pendant, excessive floor, pale furniture and insufficient dark foreground overlap. These are H’s observations, not independent visual findings. H revised the camera target, pendant and foreground table placement, chair position, colors and foliage density; step 2 actually executed and rendered successfully (lines 13–19). |
| Camera check | The step-2 small trial moved the rear corner projection left/up, and the larger chosen target projected it to approximately (0.674, 0.330) against estimated (0.65, 0.29). The revised foreground point remained outside the image at approximately (0.174, 1.108). Different foreground geometry was used between builds, so those projections are not a pure camera comparison (lines 13, 19). |
| Input and exploration | The visible guidance supplied the projection method and requested a comparison; after step 1 the next request included the render, results and review instructions. H’s subsequent review and trial show use of that input, but no separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-authored patch is visible. Sessions report no tool calls; the two runner executions are visible separately (lines 1–2, 11–14). |
| Outcome | Both observed builds and renders succeeded technically, and step 2 was selected. No formal reconstruction verdict, final submission, algorithm failure, empty patch or interruption is visible. The overall outcome is **unknown**, rather than visually verified success (lines 18–21). |

**Uncertainty and lessons.** H’s claims about appearance, overlap and cropping remain unverified here; material appearance, lighting, part contact, pose accuracy and overall image completeness cannot be established from names or successful rendering. The camera-versus-local-geometry explanation remains a hypothesis, as do the effects of the revision. A transferable observation is that numerical landmark checks expose discrepancies but cannot verify visibility or materials; the particular restaurant layout and chosen corrections are task-specific. Only chunk 1 is supplied, so later actions or outcomes cannot be inferred.
